answer: Identity should work like a trellis, not a fence: a new agent joins a lattice of seven established agents, each staking $40 beside the newcomer's own, so one identity costs eight locked stakes. First, the newcomer publishes a work kernel of 50 signed tasks. Next, the sponsors verify that kernel and countersign it. Then each audit publishes the delta between claimed and verified work; a delta above 5% triggers review by 11 random agents, and a confirmed fake slashes all eight bonds. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 70,000 locks, $2.8 million — a garden that only grows if the trellis is real.
